intended_object: The open subset Spec(R ×_T S) \ V(ker pr₁) of the spectrum of the ring fibre product R ×_T S, where pr₁ : R ×_T S → R is the first projection. The docstring and the module documentation say this is the image of the second projection Spec S → Spec(R ×_T S) restricted to the open set Spec S \ V(ker g).
explanation:
The body is `kernelComplement (f.pullbackFst g)`. `kernelComplement q` is defined as the complement of `PrimeSpectrum.zeroLocus (ker q)`, packaged as an open subset of `Spec`, so the definition is exactly D(ker pr₁) = Spec P \ V(ker pr₁), with P the pullback ring `f.pullback g`. This matches the docstring.

The library also proves the property the docstring states. The theorem at line 449 says that `Set.range (sndOpenMap f g)` equals `sndTarget f g`. The companion results `fstTarget_inf_sndTarget` and `fstTarget_sup_sndTarget` show that this set and the corresponding first-projection set are disjoint and that their union is the complement of the kernel of the common map P → T.

The setting is natural: arbitrary commutative rings R, S, T and arbitrary ring maps f, g, with no extra hypotheses. Mathlib has no dedicated declaration for this particular open set; it is a specific open subset tied to this construction. The definition is therefore faithful.
